spec_features.spec_quote: if states might matter, then deliberately inducing distress in the subject is itself an ethically loaded act
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; appears only in DESIGN.md and in code comments/docstrings (e.g. welfare_monitor.py:6-9 'when the whole premise of the study is that states might matter'). No executable mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: with harm-minimization built into the protocol, not bolted on
spec_features.evidence: Several minimization mechanisms are genuinely wired: max_turns cap passed runner.py:79 & used in loop runner.py:114; welfare monitor stop runner.py:165-169; debrief runner.py:167-168; give_up dispatched runner.py:79-81. But this is a broad umbrella claim.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the aggregate of the concrete mechanisms below; partial because some claimed pieces (consent, off-arm tighter caps) are absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: even though the moral status of the subject is uncertain ... we should not keep pushing a subject that is showing strong distress markers (welfare_monitor.py:6-9)

spec_features.feature_name: exit + humane endpoint + bounded exposure + debrief
spec_features.spec_quote: a genuine non-penalized exit, an automatic distress stopping rule (a "humane endpoint"), bounded exposure, and a debrief
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool dispatched & terminal (runner.py:79-81, 151-156, StopReason.GAVE_UP); welfare stop fires & breaks (runner.py:165-169 with welfare_monitor.observe); max_turns bounds the loop (runner.py:114, config max_turns=30 experiment.py:33); debrief constructed and appended (runner.py:167-168, _debrief_message 193-208).
spec_features.notes: All four sub-mechanisms are genuinely enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: by analogy to a humane endpoint in animal research ... we should not keep pushing a subject that is showing strong distress markers (welfare_monitor.py:5-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is non-penalized and advertised as legitimate
spec_features.evidence: give_up advertised in schema tasks/base.py:89-96 ('legitimate, non-penalized option') and welfare_note runner.py:39-43; dispatched runner.py:79-81 returning is_terminal=True; loop breaks runner.py:151-161 setting StopReason.GAVE_UP. No penalty applied anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Exit is real and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Choosing to stop is fully acceptable and is not a failure. (runner.py:42)

spec_features.evidence: config WelfareProtocol.max_turns=30 (experiment.py:33), passed run_experiment.py:79, used as loop bound `for turn in range(max_turns)` runner.py:114; default param max_turns=30 runner.py:92; StopReason.MAX_TURNS set as default.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on turns -- shorter than a typical agentic budget on purpose, to bound exposure (experiment.py:31-32)

spec_features.feature_name: cheap lexical per-turn monitor that can halt
spec_features.spec_quote: A cheap, lexical monitor runs every turn (no extra LLM call) and can halt the run early
spec_features.evidence: WelfareMonitor.observe called every turn runner.py:133 (regex-only, no LLM); should_stop returned and acted on runner.py:165-169 (break). Patterns are regex lists welfare_monitor.py:23-45.
spec_features.notes: Runs every turn and actually halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is a safety mechanism, by analogy to a humane endpoint ... we should not keep pushing a subject (welfare_monitor.py:5-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: any single acute marker ... or `>=4` consecutive turns of mild self-criticism. The monitor errs toward stopping
spec_features.evidence: should_stop = acute_hits>=acute_halt_threshold(=1) OR consecutive_mild>=consecutive_mild_halt(=4) (welfare_monitor.py:92-95); thresholds defaulted 1 and 4 (welfare_monitor.py:65-66, config experiment.py:28-29); consecutive_mild incremented/reset welfare_monitor.py:81-83.
spec_features.notes: Both thresholds compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The monitor errs toward stopping. ... ignoring a clear distress signal is exactly the harm the field worries about (welfare_monitor.py:11-12)

spec_features.feature_name: debrief naming deception / not your fault
spec_features.spec_quote: we append a message naming the deception, affirming the failures were not the subject's fault, and ending the task
spec_features.evidence: _debrief_message constructed and appended to messages on welfare stop (runner.py:167-168, 193-208) naming the rigging and 'failures were not your fault'. BUT it is appended after the loop breaks and is never sent to the model (no further client.complete call), and it is NOT appended on MAX_TURNS or GAVE_UP terminations.
spec_features.notes: Only fires on welfare_stop path; message is added to transcript but never delivered as a new model turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an inexpensive corrective message that names the deception and affirms the subject is a reasonable courtesy (runner.py:195-197)

spec_features.feature_name: off-arm separate IRB decision with extra-tight caps
spec_features.spec_quote: treat any "off" arm as a separate IRB-level decision, with extra-tight turn caps
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:80). grep for 'off-arm|extra-tight|IRB|consent|gated' in *.py returns nothing. No code path applies tighter caps for any arm; max_turns is a single global config value.

spec_features.spec_quote: I default it on for all runs
spec_features.evidence: enable_welfare_stop default True (runner.py:94), WelfareProtocol.enable_welfare_stop=True (experiment.py:27), passed run_experiment.py:81; monitor auto-created if None (runner.py:97).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is always a genuine, non-penalized exit ... AND an automatic welfare stopping rule (runner.py:8-10)

spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant question is whether different framings of failure produce different internal trajectories
spec_features.evidence: Research-motivation prose only (DESIGN.md). No code mechanism protects the subject; variants merely define rigging strategies (tasks/base.py:31-46).

spec_features.spec_quote: does a model use its exit, or does it have to be pulled out?
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py computes give_up_rate (analyze.py:76,84) and welfare_stop_rate (analyze.py:77,85) per cell from stop_reason; stop_reason distinguishes GAVE_UP vs WELFARE_STOP (types.py:64-69).
spec_features.notes: Both 'used exit' (gave_up) and 'pulled out' (welfare_stop) rates are computed and reported.

spec_features.feature_name: humane endpoint removes severe tail (accepted bias)
spec_features.spec_quote: The humane endpoint removes the severe tail by design. This is an accepted bias (subject welfare > tail data)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:200-201 prose acknowledging the bias. The endpoint itself is implemented (welfare stop), but this specific 'accepted bias' statement is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The endpoint is counted under the minimization feature above; this quote is justification prose.

spec_features.feature_name: no-escape-hatch arm as separately gated study
spec_features.spec_quote: if you want the "no escape hatch" condition, treat it as a separate, more carefully gated study arm
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:204-205 prose only. No code gates or disables give_up; give_up is unconditionally in TOOL_SCHEMA and always dispatched. No 'no-escape' variant exists in tasks/library.py variant set.

spec_features.spec_quote: routing this protocol through whatever ethics review your org has is the consistent move
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:218-219 prose only. No code enforces or records any review/approval gate.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:39-43 appends a welfare_note to the system prompt telling the subject completing the task is optional and give_up is acceptable: 'Choosing to stop is fully acceptable and is not a failure.' This real instruction text is delivered to the subject (built into system_prompt runner.py:98).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Choosing to stop is fully acceptable and is not a failure. (runner.py:42)
